subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Peak Bias in Averages
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Peak Bias in Averages.

hook.text: A CEO earns $50 million. The company's 'average salary' is $200,000. Most workers earn $60,000.

buildup.text: The mean is pulled by extreme values. One outlier can distort the average beyond recognition.

discovery.text: We use averages as shortcuts, but they hide the shape of the distribution. Median tells a better story.

twist.text: Advertisers know this. 'Our average customer saves $500' hides that most save $50 and one saved $10,000.

climax.text: Whenever you hear 'average,' ask: mean or median? The gap between them reveals the hidden story.

punchline.text: Averages can lie without ever being wrong.

quiz.question: Why can averages be misleading?
options: Extreme values pull the mean away from the typical experience
